images.caption: Northwest façade of Chambord castle. Built between 1519 and 1547 by François I, it was heavily extended afterwards by Henri II and Louis XIV to its final shape we know well today. Chambord castle is an example of Renaissance architecture. It is also the largest castle of the Loire valley, measuring 156m long and topping 56m height. A UNESCO world heritage site since 1981.
images.alt: Northwest façade of Chambord castle. Built between 1519 and 1547 by François I, it was heavily extended afterwards by Henri II and Louis XIV to its final shape we know well today. Chambord castle is an example of Renaissance architecture. It is also the largest castle of the Loire valley, measuring 156m long and topping 56m height. A UNESCO world heritage site since 1981.

images.filename: Gaobei village - seen from S319 - Chengqi Lou - DSCF3176.JPG
images.caption: Chengqi Lou, with the slopes of Jin Mt in the background, and vegetable gardens in the foreground. The tulou is seen from highway S319, which runs a few hundreds of meters to the south of the building. In front of the building we see the backs of souvenir vendors' stalls, which face the square in front of the building. The western wall of Shize Lou (a square tulou) is at right. (Highly zoomed in).
